successors.name: Zhili clique
successors.text: the provinces 'eventually annexed by the Zhili clique by the summer of 1924'

ledger.x: 1916: the Anhui clique forms around Duan Qirui.

1919 (bridging): the page's table says Xu Shuzheng 'Led expedition that reconquered Mongolia and temporarily brought it back under control'; only the Border Defence Army / National Stabilisation Army divisions are dated '1919-1920', so the year is the researcher's reading, not a page date.
ledger.cpn: Great Mongol State (Bogd Khanate of Mongolia)

ledger.x: 14 July 1920: the Zhili-Anhui War begins ('July 14, 1920 - July 23, 1920'); the page names Zhuozhou, Gaobei, Beicang, Langfang and Nanyuan.
23 July 1920: the Anhui clique is beaten.
1920 (bridging): the Anhui expedition's hold on Mongolia ends with the clique's defeat; the pages opened date neither the withdrawal nor the Soviet and Ungern events of 1921.
ledger.cpn: Great Mongol State (Bogd Khanate of Mongolia)

ledger.x: By summer 1924 (bridging): all the Anhui provinces 'were eventually annexed by the Zhili clique by the summer of 1924'; the page dates none of them (Zhang Guangjian's Gansu governorship ends in 1920 in its table).
1925: the Anhui clique has no province left.

wars.name: Zhili-Anhui War
wars.outcome: Zhili and Fengtian victory: 'Destruction of the Anhui clique'; Duan Qirui resigned on 19 July 1920.

wars.name: First Jiangsu-Zhejiang War
wars.outcome: Anhui defeat on 12 October 1924: Zhejiang and Shanghai pass to Sun Chuanfang and the Zhili clique.

certainty.note: Provinces governed through subservient governors and garrisons; no page gives a boundary other than whole provinces.
